mission_03: You have implemented Siamese Networks for few-shot learning, a pairwise comparison approach that learns to measure similarity between examples. The contrastive loss creates an embedding space where same-class examples cluster together while different-class examples are pushed apart by at least the margin distance. Unlike prototype-based methods that aggregate support examples into class representatives, Siamese networks compare the query directly to each support example, making them more flexible for irregular class distributions. The shared-weight architecture is key — both inputs are processed identically, ensuring the similarity measure is symmetric. Siamese networks have been extended to triplet loss (adding a third anchor example), relation networks (learning the similarity function), and matching networks (attention-based comparison).
